title: Product integrability criterion and Fubini interchange
statement:
Use $\mathbf R$ [def-weil-field]. Let $(X,\Sigma_X,\mu)$ and $(Y,\Sigma_Y,
u)$ be sigma-finite measure spaces and let $E$ be a real Banach space. A function is Bochner integrable if it is almost everywhere strongly measurable and its norm has finite Lebesgue integral. For every almost everywhere strongly measurable $F:X	imes Y	o E$, one has
$$F\in L^1(\mu	imes
u)\ \Longleftrightarrow\  igl(F(x,\cdot)\in L^1(
u)	ext{ for }\mu	ext{-almost every }x igr)\ 	ext{and}\ \left(x\mapsto\int_Y\|F(x,y)\|\,d
u(y)ight)\in L^1(\mu).$$
If $F$ is Bochner integrable on the product, its iterated Bochner integrals satisfy
$$\int_X\left(\int_Y F(x,y)\,d
u(y)ight)d\mu(x)=\int_Y\left(\int_X F(x,y)\,d\mu(x)ight)d
u(y).$$
